req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the index page (GET /) renders each post's author username alongside the post. The pre-loaded dataset gives us deterministic rows: post 20 (author_id=1, username='Rahul'), post 19 (author_id=1, username='Rahul'), post 18 (author_id=1, username='Rahul'), post 1 (author_id=5, username='James'), post 17 (author_id=3, username='Ishaan'), post 7 (author_id=2, username='Anjali'), etc. Tests cover: (EP/positive) multiple distinct usernames appear in the response body; (NEG/negative) a username that does NOT exist in the dataset is absent; (BVA/boundary) the most-recent post (post 20, 'Rahul', 2025-04-01) and the oldest post (post 8, 'Rahul', 2024-11-03) both have their author rendered — boundary of the ORDER BY created DESC sort. Additional tests assert exact HTTP 200 status and that all five distinct author usernames present in the post table appear.

tests.name: test_index_shows_author_username_positive
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 20 posts and 5 users as specified
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
trace: R-FLASKR-032: index renders author username alongside each post
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_shows_author_username_positive():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_shows_author_username_positive()

import tempfile, os, sqlite3

tests.name: test_index_single_post_shows_its_author
preconditions: Database schema initialised with exactly one user and one post
actions: Insert user 'Rahul' and one post authored by Rahul
Send GET / with the Flask test client
expected: Response body contains the post title 'Solo Post'
trace: R-FLASKR-032: boundary — exactly one post must still show its author username
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

def test_index_single_post_shows_its_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        db = get_db()
        with app.open_resource('schema.sql') as f:
            db.executescript(f.read().decode('utf8'))
        db.execute(
            'INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)',
            ('Rahul', generate_password_hash('stone'))
        )
        db.execute(
            'INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
            ('Solo Post', 'Only post body.', 1)
        )
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Solo Post' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_single_post_shows_its_author()
